title: Yehudah bar Mareimar

paragraphs: Hyman says that Yehudah's father Mareimar presided at Sura after Rav Ashi, as explained in Mareimar’s entry. He describes Yehudah as a colleague of Mar bar Rav Ashi. In [Berakhot 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.45b.18-19), Yehudah bar Mareimar, Mar bar Rav Ashi and Rav Acha of Difti ate bread together. None was sufficiently distinguished above his companions to lead the blessing. They came before Mareimar, etc. The supplied notice then breaks off: “And there is…”[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The notice ends with ויש (“and there is…”), both in Hyman’s print and in the supplied Hebrew.

The linked Berakhot names Yehudah bar Mareimar, Mar bar Rav Ashi and Rav Acha of Difti. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1710&lang=en) cites the same meal and gives Yehudah Mar bar Mareimar. Hyman’s following notice has this as a separate heading.

Berakhot 45b adds that the three blessed separately and Mareimar told them that they had fulfilled the blessing but missed the joint invitation to recite it. Hyman's printed notice (vol. II, p. 565) ends at ויש. The next notice is separately headed Yehudah Mar bar Mareimar. The frozen notice's ending and Hyman's statement about Sura's succession are preserved.
